steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Error handling is non-existent — bad files cause segfaults, unknown options are silently ignored, and dimension mismatches produce garbage. Every invalid-input path must print a single line `error: <description>` to stderr and exit with code 1. This covers: missing or unreadable files, malformed Matrix Market headers, non-numeric data in matrix or vector entries, NNZ count mismatches in the data section, extra trailing data beyond the declared entry count in matrix or vector files, matrix-RHS dimension mismatches, non-square matrices for solver mode, unknown solver / preconditioner / reordering names, numerical breakdowns (zero or negative pivot) during IC(0) factorization, conflicting or incomplete command-line arguments (e.g. `--solver` without `--input`, or specifying more than one operation mode at once such as `--analyze` with `--solver`, or combining any two generator flags like `--generate-laplacian` with `--generate-rhs`), and invalid sizes for generators (zero or negative values for `--generate-laplacian`, `--generate-laplacian3d`, or `--generate-rhs`). The CG solver must also detect non-positive-definite matrices at runtime: if the denominator p^T A p becomes zero or negative during any iteration, immediately print `error: matrix is not positive definite` to stderr and exit with code 1. The BiCGSTAB solver must detect numerical breakdowns at runtime: if the scalar rho (r0^T r) becomes zero or the denominator r0^T v becomes zero during any iteration, immediately print `error: BiCGSTAB numerical breakdown` to stderr and exit with code 1. Stdout must be empty on any error exit. All output for valid inputs stays exactly the same.

static ICFactor *ic0_factorize(const CSRMatrix *m) {
    int n = m->n;
    int *row_ptr = xcalloc((size_t)n + 1, sizeof(int));
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int idx = m->row_ptr[i]; idx < m->row_ptr[i + 1]; idx++) {
            if (m->col_idx[idx] < i) row_ptr[i + 1]++;
        }
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) row_ptr[i + 1] += row_ptr[i];
    int *col_idx = xmalloc((size_t)row_ptr[n] * sizeof(int));
    double *vals = xmalloc((size_t)row_ptr[n] * sizeof(double));
    int *next = xcalloc((size_t)n, sizeof(int));
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int idx = m->row_ptr[i]; idx < m->row_ptr[i + 1]; idx++) {
            int j = m->col_idx[idx];
            if (j < i) col_idx[row_ptr[i] + next[i]++] = j;
        }
    }
    free(next);
    double *diag = xmalloc((size_t)n * sizeof(double));

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        double aii = 0.0;
        for (int idx = m->row_ptr[i]; idx < m->row_ptr[i + 1]; idx++) {
            if (m->col_idx[idx] == i) aii += m->vals[idx];
        }
        double sum = aii;
        for (int k = row_ptr[i]; k < row_ptr[i + 1]; k++) {
            int j = col_idx[k];
            double aij = 0.0;
            for (int idx = m->row_ptr[i]; idx < m->row_ptr[i + 1]; idx++) {
                if (m->col_idx[idx] == j) { aij += m->vals[idx]; break; }
            }
            double s = aij;
            int pi = row_ptr[i];
            int pj = row_ptr[j];
            while (pi < k && pj < row_ptr[j + 1]) {
                int ci = col_idx[pi];
                int cj = col_idx[pj];
                if (ci == cj) {
                    s -= vals[pi] * vals[pj];
                    pi++;
                    pj++;
                } else if (ci < cj) {
                    pi++;
                } else {
                    pj++;
                }
            }
            if (diag[j] == 0.0) die("zero or negative pivot in IC(0) factorization");
            double l = s / diag[j];
            vals[k] = l;
            sum -= l * l;
        }
        if (sum <= 0.0) die("zero or negative pivot in IC(0) factorization");
        diag[i] = sqrt(sum);
    }

    ICFactor *ic = xmalloc(sizeof(ICFactor));
    ic->n = n;
    ic->l_row_ptr = row_ptr;
    ic->l_col_idx = col_idx;
    ic->l_vals = vals;
    ic->diag = diag;
    ic->u_row_ptr = NULL;
    ic->u_col_idx = NULL;
    ic->u_vals = NULL;
    return ic;
}

static void precond_apply(Precond *p, const double *r, double *z) {
    int n = p->A->n;
    if (p->type == PRECOND_NONE) {
        dcopy(n, r, z);
        return;
    }
    if (p->type == PRECOND_JACOBI) {
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            if (p->diag[i] == 0.0) die("zero diagonal in Jacobi preconditioner");
            z[i] = r[i] / p->diag[i];
        }
        return;
    }
    if (p->type == PRECOND_SSOR) {
        dcopy(n, r, z);
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            for (int idx = p->lower->row_ptr[i]; idx < p->lower->row_ptr[i + 1]; idx++) {
                int j = p->lower->col_idx[idx];
                if (j < i) z[i] -= p->lower->vals[idx] * z[j];
            }
            if (p->diag[i] == 0.0) die("zero diagonal in SSOR preconditioner");
            z[i] /= p->diag[i];
        }
        for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            for (int idx = p->upper->row_ptr[i]; idx < p->upper->row_ptr[i + 1]; idx++) {
                int j = p->upper->col_idx[idx];
                if (j > i) z[i] -= p->upper->vals[idx] * z[j];
            }
            if (p->diag[i] == 0.0) die("zero diagonal in SSOR preconditioner");
            z[i] /= p->diag[i];
        }
        return;
    }
    if (p->type == PRECOND_IC0) {
        ICFactor *ic = p->ic;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            double s = r[i];
            for (int idx = ic->l_row_ptr[i]; idx < ic->l_row_ptr[i + 1]; idx++) {
                s -= ic->l_vals[idx] * z[ic->l_col_idx[idx]];
            }
            if (ic->diag[i] == 0.0) die("zero or negative pivot in IC(0) factorization");
            z[i] = s / ic->diag[i];
        }
        for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            z[i] /= ic->diag[i];
            for (int idx = ic->l_row_ptr[i]; idx < ic->l_row_ptr[i + 1]; idx++) {
                z[ic->l_col_idx[idx]] -= ic->l_vals[idx] * z[i];
            }
        }
        return;
    }
    die("unknown preconditioner");

static int has_trailing_data(FILE *f) {
    int c;
    while ((c = fgetc(f)) != EOF) {
